children.blurb: Funder formatting and compliance covers the rules a funding body sets for how a proposal must look, what it must contain, and how it must be submitted.

children.name: Budgets and Allowable Costs
children.blurb: A grant budget is the itemized plan for how money will be spent over the life of a project, and allowable costs are the expenses a sponsor has agreed to reimburse.

children.name: Finding Collaborators
children.blurb: Finding collaborators for grant proposals in AI research means identifying people whose expertise, resources, or institutional roles complement a proposed project.

children.name: Predicting Proposal Success
children.blurb: Predicting proposal success uses machine learning to estimate the likelihood that a grant application will be funded, based on proposal text, applicant history, funder priorities, and past review patterns.

sections.body: Grant proposals and funding is the work of turning a research idea into a persuasive, compliant request for money. AI now helps draft narrative sections from prior publications, check formatting against funder rules, assemble budgets from allowable cost categories, suggest potential collaborators from publication and project records, and estimate the odds that a proposal will be funded. In practice these tools do not write a winning proposal on their own. They retrieve and reorganize text, flag missing sections, compare budget lines to agency guidance, and rank possible partners by shared topics or past work. A researcher can draw on the site's 135 research papers as source material for a proposal narrative. The human still decides the argument, the scope, and the promise.
sections.heading: What this covers

sections.body: Some parts are well supported by software. Formatting checks, reference management, budget arithmetic, and collaborator search are routine, and language models can produce readable drafts from a set of papers. Proposal success prediction is much harder because review outcomes depend on panel composition, funding priorities, and unstated criteria that historical data may not capture. AI cannot verify that a claim is novel, that a cost is allowable under a specific program, or that a collaborator will agree to the work. Confidentiality, conflicts of interest, and agency specific rules also limit what can be automated. The honest limit is that these systems assist with preparation and triage, not with the judgment that makes a proposal credible.
sections.heading: Where the work stands

sections.body: The pages under this section follow the proposal lifecycle. Drafting Proposals from Past Work covers how to turn earlier papers and results into a narrative, which is the first step before any form is filled. Funder Formatting and Compliance then addresses the rules that determine whether a proposal is even reviewed, from page limits to required sections. Budgets and Allowable Costs explains how to build a cost plan that matches what a funder will pay for. Finding Collaborators looks at how to identify partners and assemble a team, while Predicting Proposal Success examines what historical data can and cannot say about the odds of an award. Read together, they show where AI can save time and where a researcher must still supply the argument, the evidence, and the final check.
